issues.source_quote: Травма, всё достоверно!... Как говорит наш дорогой шеф, в нашем деле гланое - этот самый реализм!
issues.translation_quote: An injury—make it all authentic!... As our dear boss says, the main thing in our line of work is—realism!
issues.justification: 'Травма' here is part of the criminal plan ('injury' as staged event), and 'достоверно' means believable/plausible. 'Authentic' and 'realism' are too literal and miss the comic criminal-jargon flavor: they are trying to make the fake accident look convincing.

issues.source_quote: Но и Вы, тоже едете за границу в первый раз? Нет, я никуда не еду. Мы провожаем папу!!!
issues.translation_quote: And you, are you going abroad for the first time too? No, I’m not going anywhere. We’re seeing Dad off!!!
issues.justification: The joke lands on the reporter's blunder and the family's emphatic correction. 'Seeing Dad off' is understandable, but the whole exchange reads flatter than the original and misses the brisk comedic timing of 'Мы провожаем папу!' / 'We're just seeing Daddy off!'

The line is iconic comic pseudo-foreign speech. Leaving it transliterated without any support deprives English viewers of the joke's meaning and social function: 'Russian tourist, moral character.' In subtitles, some rendering is needed for the humor to land.

issues.source_quote: Как говорит наш дорогой шеф, если человек идиот - то это надолго.
issues.translation_quote: As our beloved boss says, if a person is an idiot, it’s for a long time.
issues.justification: This famous line is rendered too literally. English 'it's for a long time' is unnatural and misses the aphoristic punch; something like 'that's for life' or 'he'll stay one' would better preserve the comic sting.

issues.source_quote: Лёгким движением руки брюки превращаются... превращаются брюки... в элегантные шорты!
issues.translation_quote: With a slight movement of the hand, the trousers turn into... the trousers turn into... the trousers turn into... elegant shorts!
issues.justification: This is a set-piece gag whose rhythm matters. The literal wording is clunky and fails to reproduce the showman patter and buildup of the joke; the comic effect is significantly weakened.

issues.translation_quote: ice cream for the kids, flowers for his woman
issues.justification: 'Его бабе' refers to his wife/woman in coarse slang singular, while 'дитям' is comic colloquial plural. Rendering it as 'his woman' is jarringly American-sounding and shifts the social/era flavor; the stylized criminal instruction is distorted.

issues.source_quote: Наши люди в булочную на такси не ездят!
issues.translation_quote: Our people don’t take taxis to the bakery!
issues.justification: This famous line is translated semantically, but the colloquial-cultural punch is dulled. 'Our people' sounds stilted in English without reproducing the insider, self-mocking Soviet communal tone.

issues.source_quote: Шампанское по утрам пьют или аристократы, или дегенераты!
issues.translation_quote: Champagne in the morning is drunk either by aristocrats or degenerates!
issues.justification: This well-known comic line is rendered too literally and awkwardly ('is drunk'). The translation fails to preserve its crisp epigrammatic punch.

issues.source_quote: Не виноватая я! Он сам пришёл!
issues.translation_quote: It’s not my fault! He came himself!
issues.justification: The line is intentionally colloquial and theatrically self-justifying. 'He came himself' is unidiomatic in English and loses the comic resonance; the joke does not land.

issues.translation_quote: They’re removing the cast—the client is leaving.
issues.justification: This catchphrase is translated literally but without the clipped, deadpan criminal-jargon wit that makes it memorable. The humorous impact is significantly reduced.

issues.source_quote: закрытый перелом... Потерял сознание, очнулся - гипс
issues.translation_quote: a closed fracture... Lost consciousness, came to— a cast
issues.justification: This recurring formula is mostly preserved, but 'came to—a cast' remains awkwardly literal every time. A more idiomatic refrain would better carry the running gag.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты жил на одну зарплату!
issues.translation_quote: May you live on one salary!
issues.justification: A famous curse in Soviet context. The literal translation is accurate, but without adaptation the irony may not be fully clear to English viewers.
